education.content:
Hendrik Bessembinder's 2018 study of 26,000 US stocks from 1926 to 2016 found that just 4% of listed companies accounted for the entire net wealth creation above Treasury bills.

The median stock underperformed T-bills over its lifetime. The mean outperformed. That gap is the entire argument for concentrated, high-conviction portfolios over diversified index replication.

Our system targets the 4%. Thirteen positions. Six structural forces. The maths only works if each position has asymmetric upside potential and defined downside boundaries. Cash floors, catalyst calendars, systematic exits.

Bessembinder's conclusion: broad diversification guarantees average. Concentration with discipline is the only path to outlier returns.

Most investors size positions by conviction alone. High conviction, big position. Low conviction, small position.

We size by a different variable: outcome distribution.

A stock with a binary catalyst (FDA decision, trial readout) gets a smaller allocation regardless of conviction. A stock with a cash floor and multiple re-rating paths gets a larger one. Conviction determines whether we enter. Distribution shape determines how much.

$CYRX at $9.67 with $8.25 cash floor and seven re-rating methods: full T2 allocation. $NAMS at $34.76 with a single binary CVOT readout that determines 80% of future value: half-size T3. Same conviction score. Different allocation logic.

The system prices the shape of the payoff, not the strength of the opinion.

What does it mean when a stock trades below its cash value?

Cryoport has $411M in cash and equivalents. Market cap: roughly $480M. Enterprise value: $70M. That means the market assigns $70M of value to a business generating $192M in annual revenue with 70% market share in CGT logistics.

This is not "cheap." This is the market pricing in probable failure to reach profitability. The implied probability: roughly 56% that the business never earns a sustained dollar.

We disagree. The demonstrated $12M annual EBITDA improvement trajectory and nine pending therapy approvals in 2026 suggest 75% probability of profitability by H2 2026. The gap between 56% implied failure and our 25% estimate is the entire position thesis.

Q1 results: Monday after close.

O'Shaughnessy Asset Management studied 63 years of US stock returns and found that the single strongest predictor of 12-month forward returns was not earnings growth, not analyst upgrades, not insider buying.

It was price momentum combined with value. Stocks in the cheapest quintile by price-to-sales that also showed six-month price momentum outperformed the market by 5.2 percentage points annually.

Neither factor worked alone at that magnitude. Momentum without value chased expensive stocks into reversals. Value without momentum caught falling knives.

Our screening system combines both: structural momentum confirmation plus fundamental value gates. The academic evidence spans six decades. The application is real-time.

scanner.content:
Last Friday's screening: 1,279 tickers loaded across US exchanges.

30 showed momentum inflection signals. 54 confirmed trend acceleration. 18 cleared the combined filter chain across six distinct structural themes.

Three advanced to full forensic analysis. Three cleared. Fifteen were watchlisted for timing or thesis gaps. The rest: eliminated.

98.6% rejection rate. 1,261 stocks told no. That is not a bug in the system. That is the system.

This week we screened a luxury watch retailer showing momentum confirmation and institutional accumulation signals.

We walked away in under sixty seconds.

No structural force alignment. No identifiable catalyst within 90 days. Revenue declining 8% year over year. The momentum signal was real. It was also meaningless without a thesis underneath it.

Momentum confirmation is Gate 1. It is necessary but not sufficient. Twelve more stocks were eliminated at the same stage: movie exhibition, community banking, hospitality REITs, specialty chemicals. Momentum without structural backing is noise.

Six themes scored from the W16 scan:

Two rated PRIME (composite above 8.0): navy submarine hardware manufacturing and CAR-T autoimmune therapy. Both have funded catalysts within 90 days and capital flowing.

One rated PRIME: oral CETP cardiovascular (8.15 composite, but binary risk keeps allocation small).

Two INVESTABLE: CGT cold chain logistics and EM cross-border payments. Viable but need earnings confirmation or timing improvement.

The scanner does not chase narrative or sector rotation headlines. It scores catalyst density, institutional momentum, crowding risk, and forward runway. This week, biotech dominated. Next week may look entirely different.
